2026-11-17.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting AS 2 – What goes into the cost of inventory (and what never does) • Cost of purchase: price + import duties + non-recoverable taxes + freight and handling, LESS trade discounts and rebates. GST for which ITC is available is NOT part of cost. • Cost of conversion: direct labour + systematic allocation of fixed and variable production overheads. • Fixed production overheads are allocated on normal capacity. Overheads not absorbed due to low production go to P&L in that period. • Always excluded: abnormal wastage, storage costs (unless needed in production before a further stage), admin overheads not related to production, selling costs. • Valuation: lower of cost and net realisable value. Materials held for production are NOT written down if the finished goods will sell at or above cost. 📝 Exam tip: Normal transit loss is absorbed by good units (it raises the cost per kg). Abnormal loss goes to P&L. 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.
2026-11-17.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Auditing & Ethics SA 500 – Which audit evidence is more reliable? • Sufficiency = quantity of evidence. Appropriateness = quality (relevance + reliability). • Evidence from independent external sources is more reliable than evidence generated inside the entity. • Internally generated evidence is more reliable when the related controls are effective. • Evidence obtained directly by the auditor (e.g. observation of a control) beats evidence obtained indirectly or by inference (e.g. inquiry). • Documentary evidence beats oral representations, and originals beat photocopies, faxes or scanned copies. 📝 Exam tip: More evidence cannot make up for poor-quality evidence. Sufficiency and appropriateness work together. 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.

2026-11-18.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – Income Tax Residential status of an individual – Sec 6 in one view • Resident if EITHER: (a) in India 182 days or more in the P.Y., OR (b) 60 days or more in the P.Y. AND 365 days or more in the 4 preceding P.Ys. • 60 days becomes 182 days for an Indian citizen leaving India for employment or as crew of an Indian ship, and for an Indian citizen/PIO visiting India. • Exception: for a visiting Indian citizen/PIO whose total income (other than foreign-source income) exceeds ₹15 lakh, the 60 days becomes 120 days (with 365 in 4 years). Such a person is RNOR. • Deemed resident – Sec 6(1A): Indian citizen, total income (other than foreign source) above ₹15 lakh, not liable to tax in any other country. Always RNOR. • ROR needs both: resident in at least 2 of the 10 preceding P.Ys AND 730 days or more in the 7 preceding P.Ys. Otherwise RNOR. 📝 Exam tip: For ship crew, the days between joining and signing off as per the Continuous Discharge Certificate are excluded from the stay in India. 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.
2026-11-18.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Cost & Management Accounting Process costing – Normal loss, abnormal loss and abnormal gain • Normal loss = expected loss (a % of input). Its cost is absorbed by good units, and its scrap value is credited to the process account. • Cost per unit = (total cost − scrap value of normal loss) ÷ (input − normal loss units). • Abnormal loss = actual loss above normal. It is valued at the same cost per unit as good output and moved to Costing P&L (less its scrap value). • Abnormal gain = actual loss below normal. It is debited to the process account at the normal cost per unit. • Abnormal gain reduces the normal-loss scrap recovery, so the 'lost' scrap value is charged to the Abnormal Gain account. 📝 Exam tip: Always compute normal loss on the input of THAT process, not on the original material. 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.

2026-11-19.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – GST Sec 15 – Value of supply: what to add and what to leave out • Start with the transaction value: price actually paid or payable, parties not related, and price the sole consideration. • Add: taxes, duties and fees other than GST; amounts the supplier owed but the recipient paid; incidental expenses (packing, commission) charged by the supplier; interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment. • Add subsidies directly linked to the price, EXCEPT subsidies from the Central or State Government, which are excluded. • Exclude discounts given before or at the time of supply if recorded in the invoice. • Post-supply discounts are excluded only if agreed before the supply, linked to specific invoices, and the recipient has reversed the matching ITC. 📝 Exam tip: A late fee that is waived was never charged, so it does not enter the value. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.
2026-11-19.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Financial Management Cost of capital – Ke, Kd and WACC basics • CAPM: Ke = Rf + β (Rm − Rf). β measures systematic (market) risk only. • Cost of debt (after tax): Kd = Interest × (1 − tax rate). For redeemable debt, use the approximate YTM formula. • WACC = Σ (weight × cost). Market-value weights are preferred over book-value weights. • Project risk: if a project is riskier than the firm, use the project's own beta to get a project-specific discount rate. • Flotation cost raises the cost of new equity: Ke = D1 ÷ (P0 − flotation cost) + g. 📝 Exam tip: Using the firm's WACC for a riskier project can wrongly accept a value-destroying project. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.

2026-11-20.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Corporate & Other Laws Sec 96 – Annual General Meeting deadlines • First AGM: within 9 months from the close of the first financial year. No other AGM is needed in the year of incorporation. • Later AGMs: within 6 months from the close of the financial year, AND the gap between two AGMs cannot exceed 15 months. • Extension: the Registrar may extend the time by up to 3 months for special reasons, but NOT for the first AGM. • Time: during business hours (9 AM to 6 PM) on a day that is not a national holiday. • Place: the registered office or another place in the same city, town or village where the registered office is situated. 📝 Exam tip: Always check both limits (6 months AND 15 months). Many MCQs break only one of them. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!
2026-11-20.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Strategic Management Ansoff's growth matrix • Market penetration – existing products, existing markets (sell more to current customers). • Market development – existing products, new markets (new regions, new segments). • Product development – new products, existing markets. • Diversification – new products, new markets (the riskiest option). • Risk rises as the firm moves away from what it already knows: its products and its customers. 📝 Exam tip: First ask: is the product new? Is the market new? The answer to those two questions gives the quadrant. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!

2026-11-21.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting AS 10 – Treatment of revaluation increases and decreases • Increase: credited to Revaluation Surplus, EXCEPT to the extent it reverses an earlier decrease of the same asset charged to P&L. That part goes to P&L. • Decrease: charged to P&L, EXCEPT to the extent of any existing Revaluation Surplus for the same asset. That part is debited to the surplus. • Whole class: if one item is revalued, the entire class of PPE to which it belongs must be revalued. • Regularity: revaluations must be frequent enough that the carrying amount is not materially different from fair value. • Surplus transfer: the surplus may be transferred directly to Retained Earnings as the asset is used or derecognised – never through P&L. 📝 Exam tip: Think 'same asset first': reverse what went through P&L before using the surplus. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.
2026-11-21.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Auditing & Ethics SA 570 – Going concern: indicators and reporting • Financial indicators: net liability position, maturing loans with no renewal, withdrawal of creditor support, negative operating cash flows, inability to pay creditors on time. • Operating indicators: loss of key management, major market, key customer or principal supplier; labour or supply shortages; emergence of a strong competitor. • Period: evaluate management's assessment covering at least 12 months from the date of the financial statements. • Material uncertainty adequately disclosed: unmodified opinion with a separate section 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern'. • Not adequately disclosed: qualified or adverse opinion. Going concern basis inappropriate: adverse opinion. 📝 Exam tip: Management's plans must be evaluated for feasibility. An 'expectation of finance' alone is not evidence. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.

2026-11-23.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting AS 13 – Current vs long-term investments • Cost includes brokerage, fees and duties. Interest accrued before acquisition and bought cum-interest is NOT part of cost – it is a recovery of cost. • Current investments: lower of cost and fair value, computed category-wise or investment-wise – never on a global (overall portfolio) basis. • Long-term investments: at cost, less a provision for decline in value that is other than temporary. • Reclassification: long-term → current at the lower of cost and carrying amount; current → long-term at the lower of cost and fair value. • Disposal: the difference between carrying amount and net disposal proceeds goes to P&L. On partial disposal, use the average carrying amount of the holding. 📝 Exam tip: In 'ex-interest vs cum-interest' questions, split the price first: only the capital part goes into the cost of the investment. 🎯 Revise it tonight, recall it in the exam hall.
2026-11-23.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Cost & Management Accounting Marginal costing – P/V ratio, BEP and margin of safety • Contribution = Sales − Variable cost = Fixed cost + Profit. • P/V ratio = Contribution ÷ Sales × 100 = Change in profit ÷ Change in sales × 100. • BEP (units) = Fixed cost ÷ Contribution per unit. BEP (₹) = Fixed cost ÷ P/V ratio. • Margin of safety = Actual sales − BEP sales = Profit ÷ P/V ratio. • Sales for a target profit = (Fixed cost + Target profit) ÷ P/V ratio. 📝 Exam tip: When two periods' sales and profits are given, find the P/V ratio from the CHANGE first – everything else follows from it. 🎯 Revise it tonight, recall it in the exam hall.

2026-11-24.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Corporate & Other Laws Private company – Sec 2(68) and how it differs from a public company • A private company by its articles: (a) restricts the right to transfer its shares, (b) limits members to 200, and (c) prohibits any invitation to the public to subscribe to its securities. • The 200 limit excludes present employee-members and ex-employees who were members while employed and continue as members. Joint holders count as one member. • Minimum members: 2 for a private company, 7 for a public company, 1 for an OPC. • Minimum directors: 2 for a private company, 3 for a public company, 1 for an OPC. • A private company that is a subsidiary of a public company is treated as a public company, even if its articles say it is private. 📝 Exam tip: In case questions, check the subsidiary point first – it changes the answer to 'Is this a private company?' 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.
2026-11-24.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Auditing & Ethics SA 530 – Audit sampling in one view • Sampling risk: the risk that the auditor's conclusion from a sample differs from the conclusion if the whole population were tested. • Non-sampling risk: any other reason for a wrong conclusion – wrong procedure, misread evidence, missed misstatement. • Selection methods: random, systematic, monetary unit sampling and haphazard selection. Block selection is rarely appropriate. • Stratification splits the population into sub-groups with similar characteristics, so sample size can fall without raising risk. • Evaluate: project the misstatements found in the sample to the whole population and compare with tolerable misstatement. An anomaly is a misstatement shown not to represent the population. 📝 Exam tip: If the auditor cannot perform a procedure on a selected item, treat it as a deviation or misstatement – do not simply pick another item. 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.

2026-11-25.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – GST Sec 12 – Time of supply of goods • Forward charge: the earlier of (a) date of issue of invoice (or the last date by which it should have been issued u/s 31) and (b) date of receipt of payment. • Advances for goods: by notification, GST is not payable on receipt of an advance for goods. It is paid when the invoice is issued (not available to composition taxpayers). • Reverse charge – Sec 12(3): the earliest of date of receipt of goods, date of payment, and the date immediately after 30 days from the supplier's invoice. • Vouchers – Sec 12(4): date of issue of the voucher if the supply is identifiable then; otherwise the date of redemption. • Interest or late fee for delayed payment: time of supply is the date the recipient pays it. 📝 Exam tip: Up to ₹1,000 received in excess of the invoice amount: the supplier may treat the invoice date as the time of supply for that excess. 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.
2026-11-25.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Financial Management Leverages – operating, financial and combined • DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT. It measures business risk from fixed operating costs. • DFL = EBIT ÷ EBT. With preference dividend: EBIT ÷ [EBT − Preference dividend ÷ (1 − t)]. • DCL = DOL × DFL = Contribution ÷ EBT. • Meaning: a DOL of 3 means a 1% change in sales gives a 3% change in EBIT. A DFL of 2 means a 1% change in EBIT gives a 2% change in EPS. • Operating BEP: where EBIT = 0, DOL is undefined. Just above BEP, DOL is very high, so firms close to BEP carry high business risk. 📝 Exam tip: High DOL and high DFL together = very high total risk. Examiners like asking which one to reduce first. 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.

2026-11-26.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting AS 14 – Merger vs purchase • Amalgamation in the nature of merger – ALL five conditions: all assets and liabilities transferred; holders of at least 90% of equity shares (by face value) become equity shareholders of the transferee; consideration only in equity shares (cash only for fractions); business continued; no adjustment to book values except for uniform accounting policies. • If any one condition fails, it is an amalgamation in the nature of purchase. • Merger → pooling of interests: assets, liabilities and reserves are recorded at book values. Any difference goes to reserves. • Purchase → purchase method: assets and liabilities at book or fair values. Excess of consideration over net assets = goodwill (amortised over not more than 5 years unless a longer period is justified); shortfall = capital reserve. • Statutory reserves in a purchase are preserved by crediting them and debiting the Amalgamation Adjustment Reserve. 📝 Exam tip: Read the scheme for 'cash paid to shareholders' – one cash payment beyond fractions makes it a purchase. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.
2026-11-26.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Strategic Management Porter's generic strategies • Cost leadership: be the lowest-cost producer in the industry and compete on price or earn higher margins. • Differentiation: offer unique features (quality, brand, service) that customers will pay a premium for. • Focus: serve a narrow segment – either by cost focus or by differentiation focus. • Risks: cost leaders can be copied or hit by technology change; differentiators can be copied or lose the price premium; focusers can see the segment disappear. • Stuck in the middle: a firm that tries all strategies without achieving any of them usually earns below-average returns. 📝 Exam tip: In a case, look for clue words: 'lowest price', 'premium', 'niche' – then name the strategy and justify it with the facts. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.

2026-11-27.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – Income Tax Capital gains – holding period and tax rates (A.Y. 2026-27) • Long-term if held for more than 12 months for listed securities and units of equity-oriented funds, and more than 24 months for all other capital assets. • STCG u/s 111A (STT-paid equity shares and equity-oriented fund units): 20%. • LTCG u/s 112A: 12.5% on gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh in the year. • LTCG u/s 112 (other assets): 12.5% without indexation. For land or building acquired before 23 July 2024, a resident individual or HUF pays the lower of 12.5% without indexation and 20% with indexation. • Always short-term: depreciable assets (Sec 50), and specified mutual fund units and market-linked debentures (Sec 50AA). 📝 Exam tip: Count the holding period from the date of acquisition to the date of transfer – then apply the right section before any rate. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!
2026-11-27.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Cost & Management Accounting Standard costing – material variances • Material cost variance = Standard cost for actual output − Actual cost. • Price variance = (Standard price − Actual price) × Actual quantity. • Usage variance = (Standard quantity for actual output − Actual quantity) × Standard price. • Mix variance = (Revised standard quantity − Actual quantity) × Standard price. • Yield variance = (Standard quantity for actual output − Revised standard quantity) × Standard price. Check: Mix + Yield = Usage. 📝 Exam tip: Revised standard quantity = total actual quantity split in the STANDARD mix ratio. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!

2026-11-28.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Corporate & Other Laws FEMA – current account vs capital account transactions • Person resident in India – Sec 2(v): resides in India for more than 182 days in the preceding financial year (with exclusions for those who leave India for employment, business or an uncertain period). • Capital account transaction – Sec 2(e): alters the assets or liabilities (including contingent liabilities) outside India of residents, or in India of non-residents. • Current account transaction – Sec 2(j): any transaction other than a capital account transaction, e.g. foreign trade payments, interest on loans, remittances for living expenses of family abroad, foreign travel, education and medical care. • Sec 5: current account transactions are freely allowed, subject to reasonable restrictions the Central Government may impose in public interest. • Sec 6: capital account transactions are allowed only as permitted – the Central Government regulates non-debt instruments and the RBI regulates debt instruments. 📝 Exam tip: Ask one question: does it change an asset or liability across the border? Yes → capital account. No → current account. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.
2026-11-28.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Auditing & Ethics SA 580 – Written representations • Required: management confirms it has prepared the financial statements per the framework, given the auditor all information and access, and recorded all transactions. • Date: as near as practicable to, but NOT after, the date of the auditor's report. • Addressed to the auditor, as a letter of representation signed by management. • Not a substitute for other audit evidence – it supports evidence, it does not replace it. • If management refuses the required representations, or the auditor doubts their reliability because of management's integrity, the auditor issues a disclaimer of opinion. 📝 Exam tip: Written representations about specific items (e.g. intent to hold an investment) support, but never prove, the assertion. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.

2026-11-30.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting AS 22 – Deferred tax • Timing differences arise in one period and reverse later (e.g. depreciation rates differ between books and tax). They create deferred tax. • Permanent differences never reverse (e.g. a penalty disallowed for tax). No deferred tax on them. • DTA is recognised only if there is reasonable certainty of future taxable income. For unabsorbed depreciation or carried-forward losses, there must be virtual certainty supported by convincing evidence. • Measured using tax rates enacted or substantively enacted at the balance sheet date. Deferred tax is NOT discounted. • Tax holiday (e.g. 80-IA): no deferred tax for timing differences that reverse within the holiday period. 📝 Exam tip: Re-assess unrecognised DTA at every balance sheet date – it can be recognised later when certainty arrives. 🎯 Revise it tonight, recall it in the exam hall.
2026-11-30.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Financial Management NPV vs IRR – when they disagree • For independent projects with normal cash flows, NPV and IRR give the same accept/reject decision. • Conflicts arise for mutually exclusive projects due to: size disparity, different timing of cash flows, or unequal lives. • Reinvestment assumption: NPV assumes reinvestment at the cost of capital; IRR assumes reinvestment at the IRR itself – usually unrealistic. • Non-conventional cash flows (signs change more than once) can give multiple IRRs or none. • In a conflict, prefer NPV – it measures the absolute increase in wealth. MIRR fixes the reinvestment problem of IRR. 📝 Exam tip: For unequal lives, use the equivalent annual annuity (EAA) or replacement chain before comparing NPVs. 🎯 Revise it tonight, recall it in the exam hall.

2026-12-01.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – GST Sec 17(5) – Blocked credits • Motor vehicles for transport of persons with seating capacity of 13 or less (including the driver) – blocked, except when used for further supply of such vehicles, transport of passengers, or training on driving. • Food, outdoor catering, beauty treatment, health services, cosmetic surgery, life and health insurance – blocked, unless used for an outward supply of the same category or obligatory under a law for employers. • Club membership, health and fitness centre, travel benefits to employees on vacation (LTC) – blocked. • Construction of immovable property (other than plant and machinery) on own account, including works contract services – blocked, even if used in business. • Goods lost, stolen, destroyed, written off, or given as gifts or free samples, and goods or services for personal consumption – blocked. 📝 Exam tip: Plant and machinery is NOT blocked – but land, buildings and civil structures (and pipelines/telecom towers outside the factory) are not 'plant and machinery'. 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.
2026-12-01.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Cost & Management Accounting Activity Based Costing (ABC) • Idea: activities consume resources and products consume activities – so overheads are traced through activities. • Steps: identify activities → build cost pools → choose a cost driver for each → compute driver rates → charge products by drivers used. • Cost hierarchy: unit-level, batch-level, product-sustaining and facility-sustaining activities. • Drivers: transaction drivers (number of set-ups, orders) and duration drivers (set-up hours, inspection hours). • Insight: traditional absorption usually UNDER-costs low-volume, complex products and OVER-costs high-volume simple ones. 📝 Exam tip: ABC helps most when overheads are a large share of cost and products differ widely in complexity. 🎯 One concept clear today = one question right in the exam.

2026-12-02.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Corporate & Other Laws Dividend – Sec 123 and the payment timeline • Source: profits of the current year or previous years, after providing for depreciation, or money provided by the Government for payment of dividend under its guarantee. • Out of free reserves when profits are inadequate – only as per the prescribed rules (previous losses and depreciation must be set off first). • Interim dividend: declared by the Board. Final dividend: recommended by the Board, declared at the AGM. • Deposit the dividend amount in a separate bank account within 5 days of declaration. Pay within 30 days (Sec 127). • Unpaid dividend → Unpaid Dividend Account within 7 days after the 30 days (Sec 124). Unclaimed for 7 years → transferred to IEPF. 📝 Exam tip: Dividend is payable only in cash – capitalising profits as bonus shares is not a dividend. 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.
2026-12-02.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Auditing & Ethics SA 705 – Which modified opinion? • Qualified opinion: misstatements are material but NOT pervasive, or the auditor cannot get sufficient evidence and the possible effects are material but not pervasive. • Adverse opinion: misstatements are both material AND pervasive. • Disclaimer of opinion: the auditor cannot get sufficient appropriate evidence and the possible effects could be both material and pervasive. • Pervasive = not confined to specific elements, or if confined, a substantial part of the FS, or fundamental to users' understanding of the disclosures. • The report includes a 'Basis for Qualified/Adverse Opinion' or 'Basis for Disclaimer of Opinion' paragraph describing the matter. 📝 Exam tip: Two questions decide it: Is it a misstatement or a lack of evidence? Is it pervasive or not? 🎯 Small daily revisions build big marks in January.

2026-12-03.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Advanced Accounting Buy-back of shares – Sec 68, 69 and 70 • Sources: free reserves, securities premium, or proceeds of an issue of shares or securities (but NOT from an earlier issue of the same kind). • Limits: Board resolution up to 10% of paid-up capital + free reserves; special resolution up to 25%. For equity shares, the buy-back in a year cannot exceed 25% of paid-up equity capital. • Debt-equity after buy-back must not exceed 2:1 (secured and unsecured debt vs paid-up capital + free reserves). • Sec 69: when bought back out of free reserves or securities premium, transfer an amount equal to the nominal value bought back to the Capital Redemption Reserve. • Timing: complete within 1 year of the resolution; no fresh issue of the same kind for 6 months (except bonus and existing obligations); 1 year gap between two buy-backs. 📝 Exam tip: Run all three tests (shares outstanding, resources, debt-equity) – the maximum buy-back is the LOWEST of the three. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.
2026-12-03.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Strategic Management Porter's value chain • Value chain splits a firm into activities that create value, so the source of competitive advantage can be found. • Primary activities: inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing and sales, and service. • Support activities: firm infrastructure, human resource management, technology development and procurement. • Margin = value created for customers minus the cost of performing the activities. • Linkages between activities (e.g. better procurement reducing defects in operations) are often a stronger advantage than any single activity. 📝 Exam tip: In a case, map each fact to one activity – then say whether it supports cost leadership or differentiation. 🎯 Understand it once, and you won't need to mug it up.

2026-12-04.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – Income Tax New tax regime – Sec 115BAC for individuals (A.Y. 2026-27) • Slabs: up to ₹4 lakh nil; ₹4–8 lakh 5%; ₹8–12 lakh 10%; ₹12–16 lakh 15%; ₹16–20 lakh 20%; ₹20–24 lakh 25%; above ₹24 lakh 30%. • Rebate u/s 87A: up to ₹60,000 where total income does not exceed ₹12 lakh (not available on tax on special-rate income like Sec 111A/112A), with marginal relief just above ₹12 lakh. • Allowed: standard deduction ₹75,000; family pension deduction ₹25,000; Sec 80CCD(2) employer's NPS contribution; Sec 80CCH; Sec 80JJAA. • Not allowed: Sec 80C, 80D and most Chapter VI-A deductions; HRA; LTA; interest on a self-occupied house property u/s 24(b). • Default regime: applies unless the individual opts out. Without business income – choose every year in the return. With business income – opt out by Form 10-IEA, with only one chance to come back. 📝 Exam tip: Always compute the rebate before cess – health and education cess at 4% is charged on tax AFTER the rebate. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!
2026-12-04.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Cost & Management Accounting Joint products and by-products • Joint products: two or more products of significant relative value produced at the same time from the same process. • By-product: a product of relatively small value produced incidentally with the main product. • Split-off point: the stage where joint products become separately identifiable. Costs up to it are joint costs. • Apportioning joint costs: physical units method, sales value at split-off, net realisable value method, or constant gross margin method. • Further processing decision: process further only if incremental revenue exceeds incremental cost after split-off. Joint costs are irrelevant to this decision. 📝 Exam tip: By-product income can be credited to the main product's cost, shown as other income, or handled by the reverse cost method – state which one you use. 🎯 Consistency beats intensity – see you tomorrow at 9 AM!

2026-12-05.g1: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 1 📘 Taxation – GST Composition levy – Sec 10 • Eligibility: aggregate turnover in the preceding FY up to ₹1.5 crore (₹75 lakh in certain special category States). • Rates (CGST + SGST): manufacturers 1%, traders 1% (on turnover of taxable supplies), restaurants not serving alcohol 5%. • Services: a composition supplier of goods may also supply services up to 10% of turnover or ₹5 lakh, whichever is higher. A pure service provider can use Sec 10(2A) – turnover up to ₹50 lakh at 6%. • Not allowed: inter-State outward supplies, non-taxable goods, notified goods (e.g. ice cream, pan masala, tobacco), casual and non-resident taxable persons. • Conditions: cannot collect tax from customers, cannot take ITC, must issue a bill of supply, and must display 'composition taxable person' at the place of business. 📝 Exam tip: The turnover limit is checked on ALL-India aggregate turnover under the same PAN – not State-wise. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.
2026-12-05.g2: 🧠 CONCEPT OF THE DAY – Group 2 📘 Financial Management Dividend decision – Walter and Gordon models • Walter: P = [D + (r ÷ Ke) × (E − D)] ÷ Ke, where r = return on investment and Ke = cost of equity. • Walter's rule: r > Ke (growth firm) → 0% payout is best; r < Ke (declining firm) → 100% payout is best; r = Ke → payout does not matter. • Gordon: P0 = E(1 − b) ÷ (Ke − br), where b = retention ratio and g = br. • Bird-in-hand (Gordon): investors value a certain dividend today more than uncertain future gains, so Ke rises with retention. • MM approach: in perfect markets, dividend policy does not affect the value of the firm. 📝 Exam tip: In Walter questions, find r and Ke first – the optimal payout is decided before any calculation of P. 🎯 Every concept you master is a mark you protect.
